name: AutoBaggingHook
summary: Hook with automatic pruning for moving targets: objects whose scores stay low are removed from consideration over time, so the candidate set shrinks without extra input.
howItWorks: As with Hook, the user follows the moving target with a controller cursor and objects gain or lose score by their distance to it; AutoBaggingHook periodically prunes away objects with low scores, which converge faster than plain Hook in crowded, fast-moving scenes. Both build on Hook's score heuristic. Pruned distractors turn grey and semi-transparent, reducing occlusion. In a VR study (Meta Quest Pro, one controller) with molecular-dynamics-like scenes of fast, unpredictably moving objects, AutoBaggingHook was the fastest without more errors, while BaggingHook was preferred by most participants for its sense of control; both were compared with Hook.
advantages: Fastest of the three techniques tested.
No extra actions beyond following the target.
limitations: Less sense of control; fewer participants preferred it.

relationships.note: Adds automatic score-based pruning to Hook.
Faster than Hook without more errors.
